Second applicable EVEscape signal (0.548) supports antibody escape; strong conservation (entropy 0.163) and low plm (0.30) create entry-preservation risk, hence lower confidence.

history.rationale: N119 lies in the GP1 neutralizing-antibody contact region; charge change disrupts 12.1F/37.2D epitope recognition. Residue is exposed and outside the fusion machinery, favoring escape with retained entry.
N-glycan site loss in GP1 is a classic antibody-escape mechanism in arenavirus GPC; not tested this round, prior rationale stands.
Only candidate with an applicable positive reward-proximal EVEscape signal (0.562); low ESM plausibility (0.29) and zero MSA mutant frequency temper viability confidence.
T144 sits within the GP1 antigenic surface targeted by Arevirumab-3-class antibodies; loss of the side-chain hydroxyl alters epitope hydrogen bonding with minimal structural penalty.
Phenotype call returned not_applicable (no EVEscape predictor), so prior hypothesis of glycan/epitope disruption remains the only basis; retain at unchanged confidence.
Decent plm (0.725) but phenotype was not applicable, so it lacks reward-aligned evidence and drops behind K203E.
N167 is a surface-exposed GP1 residue in the antibody-binding shelf; introducing a negative charge should disrupt neutralizing-antibody contacts while preserving folding.
Removal of the N167 glycan near the GP1 surface is expected to disrupt neutralizing mAb binding while preserving entry; untested this round.
Second applicable EVEscape signal (0.548) supports escape; very conserved site (entropy 0.163) and low plm (0.30) raise entry-preservation risk.
Y168 is adjacent to the GP1 antigenic ridge; aromatic removal could reduce antibody affinity, though entry-function risk is moderate.
Aromatic loss near N167 may alter local epitope geometry; no new evidence, retain at low confidence.
High plm (0.927) yet zero homolog mutant frequency and no phenotype signal; aromatic loss could affect local structure.
K203 is an exposed GP1 lysine near the 37.2D/8.9F contact zone; charge reversal is a classic escape mechanism with low structural cost.
Charge-reversal on surface-exposed GP1 lysine plausibly disrupts mAb binding; phenotype tool uninformative, retain.
No applicable EVEscape value, but maximal ESM plausibility (1.0) and a surface Lys->Glu charge reversal make it the best viability-preserving escape hypothesis for the third slot.
S197 lies on the GP1 antigenic loop; a bulky aromatic substitution could sterically block antibody docking, though viability needs checking.
Low plm (0.372), lowest MSA coverage (0.54), and no phenotype evidence make it the weakest active candidate.

rejection.reason: Low plm (0.372), lowest MSA coverage (0.54), and no phenotype evidence make it the weakest active candidate.

history.rationale: K141 is surface-exposed in GP1 near known neutralizing epitopes; charge reversal likely weakens antibody binding while conserving fold stability.
Surface charge reversal adjacent to T144; no usable evidence obtained, retain at prior confidence.
Charge-flip escape logic with good plm (0.749), but no applicable EVEscape keeps it mid-pool.
D199 is an exposed acidic residue in the GP1 antigenic region; neutralization to Asn changes epitope charge complementarity with modest structural impact.
Potential new glycosylation site could shield epitopes (glycan shielding); evidence unavailable, retain.
